title: Nicos Weg, Episode 1: Hallo!
author: Deutsche Welle (DW Learn German)
price: Free (free account optional for progress tracking)
format: Web video series + interactive exercises; downloadable script and vocabulary PDF; podcast feed
level_stated: A1 (course continues through A2 and B1)
level_judgment: Yes, built for zero knowledge. Episode 1 is greetings only; the English interface and video carry the meaning. Reading is a minor part: it's mainly a video course with a script to read.
hook: Follow Nico, a young Spaniard who lands in Germany with nothing, across about 100 episodes. A Spanish speaker may identify with him.
snippet_de: EMMA: Oh, schön! NICO: Hm? EMMA: Die Tasche ist schön! NICO: Entschuldigung? Schön?
snippet_en: EMMA: Oh, nice! NICO: Hm? EMMA: The bag is nice! NICO: Sorry? Nice?
aids: German subtitles on video; script PDF with English vocabulary list (learngerman.dw.com/downloads/47207956/nicos-weg-eng-a1-e0-l1-manuskript-und-wortschatz.pdf); English UI; grammar pages
notes: Snippet taken from DW's official script PDF. The DW web pages are a JavaScript app, so WebFetch couldn't read them; the episode URL was confirmed through search results.

title: Harry – gefangen in der Zeit, Episode 1: Ferien im Schwarzwald
author: Deutsche Welle (DW Learn German)
format: Web animated audio drama (about 8 min per episode) + script PDFs + exercises
level_judgment: Yes. The narrator and Harry speak English and only the German bits are in German, so a true A0 can follow from day one. Read the script after watching each episode.
hook: A grumpy tourist gets struck by lightning and is stuck repeating the same day, Groundhog Day style, until he learns German. The tone is sarcastic and silly.
snippet_de: Danke, auch gut. Es ist heiß heute! — Ja, es gibt heute ein Gewitter.
snippet_en: Thanks, I'm fine too. It's hot today! — Yes, there's going to be a thunderstorm today.
aids: Script PDF with English narration (static.dw.com/downloads/61395215/harry-001-a-holiday-in-the-black-forest-manuskript-englisch.pdf), vocabulary lists, grammar pages
notes: The English-narrated format is unusually gentle for a complete beginner. Most of the script is English, so there's less German to mine per episode than in Nicos Weg.

title: Duolingo Stories: Guten Morgen! (and the rest of the German Stories sets)
author: Duolingo
price: Free (inside the Duolingo app/web; Stories unlock as you progress)
level_stated: Intro / A1.1 for Sets 1–2; A2 for Sets 3–5; B1 from Set 6
level_judgment: Yes. About 25 lines each, very short sentences, and every word is tappable. Probably the easiest real fiction for week 1–2.
hook: Each story is a one-minute sitcom gag. In this one a tired wife puts salt in her coffee.
snippet_de: Anna gibt Zucker in den Kaffee. Sie trinkt den Kaffee. Igitt! Das ist Salz!
snippet_en: Anna puts sugar in the coffee. She drinks the coffee. Yuck! That's salt!
aids: Tap-to-translate on every word, comprehension questions mid-story, full voiced audio
notes: Text copied from duome.eu's mirror of the official story; Duolingo's own story pages need a login. Duolingo has reorganised Stories into the main path, so exact access varies.

title: Die Kaffeemaschine ist kaputt
author: LingoStories
format: Web/app story with audio, quiz, vocabulary
level_judgment: Yes after about 2–3 weeks: short present-tense sentences and high-frequency words. The plots are thin.
hook: Low stakes and relatable: the office coffee machine dies on a Monday. Good for building basic vocabulary, not exciting.
snippet_de: Es ist Montagmorgen. Anna kommt früh zur Arbeit. Sie ist heute sehr müde.
snippet_en: It's Monday morning. Anna comes to work early. She is very tired today.
aids: Click any sentence for an English translation; 20-word vocabulary list per story; exercises
notes: A large A1 library. The stories seem generated to a template (many are about coffee and offices), so variety of tone is limited.

title: Kaffee im Regen
author: Love For Languages
price: Some stories free; premium membership for full access (price not stated on the page)
format: Web/app interlinear story with multi-voice audio
level_judgment: Stretch. It uses subordinate clauses (als, dass) and words like Vordach and Wettervorhersage, so it reads more like A2. Usable for an absolute beginner only because every chunk carries an English gloss.
hook: Two neighbours get stuck under an awning in the rain and end up with an espresso date.
snippet_de: An einem Mittwochmorgen verlässt Giancarlo früh seine Wohnung. Als er nach draußen tritt, merkt er, dass es regnet.
snippet_en: Early on a Wednesday morning, Giancarlo leaves his apartment. When he steps outside, he notices that it's raining.
aids: Phrase-by-phrase interlinear English gloss, full-sentence translation, 4 narrator voices, speed control 0.7–1.3x
notes: The interlinear format suits mining expressions (not just single words) for spaced repetition.

title: Der erste Tag
author: LernLaterne
price: Free plan includes 4 full stories plus the first 5 scenes of an A1 illustrated course; full access €10/month or €60/year
format: Web interactive story (choose-your-ending) with audio on paid plans
level_judgment: Not in week 1. Comfortable after about 6–8 weeks; it includes a perfect tense and weil clauses.
hook: A nervous new café waiter spills coffee on a customer's new handbag, and you pick how he handles it.
snippet_de: Simon ist nervös. Heute ist sein erster Tag im Café am Markt. Er braucht einen Job, weil er Geld für einen neuen Computer sparen will.
snippet_en: Simon is nervous. Today is his first day at the Café am Markt. He needs a job because he wants to save money for a new computer.
aids: Graded vocabulary; audio on paid plans; site also has an illustrated A1 course
notes: Branching endings are a good test of whether the learner likes interactive formats.

title: Vorstellung (and the other A1 texts)
author: Tim Seeger / Lingua.com
price: Free for this text; 10 more A1 texts are premium
format: Web text + PDF + audio + comprehension quiz
level_judgment: Yes. A classic textbook self-introduction, readable within the first 2 weeks.
hook: Honestly not gripping. It's a quick confidence win and covers core family and hobby vocabulary.
snippet_de: Mein Name ist Anna. Ich komme aus Österreich und lebe seit drei Jahren in Deutschland. Ich bin 15 Jahre alt und habe zwei Geschwister.
snippet_en: My name is Anna. I come from Austria and have lived in Germany for three years. I am 15 years old and have two siblings.
aids: Audio by several native speakers; 5-question quiz; no built-in dictionary
notes: Include it as a baseline: if this bores the learner, steer toward story or humour formats.

title: Dino lernt Deutsch 1: Café in Berlin
author: André Klein (LearnOutLive)
format: Ebook (DRM-free) and paperback; 10 short chapters, about 9,200 words
level_judgment: Readable from about week 3–4 with the glossary. Sentences are short, and some words (Wohngemeinschaft, Statistiken) are glossed.
hook: A Sicilian guy moves to Berlin, lives in a chaotic multinational flat share and tries to learn German. It's self-deprecating and wry, and the Mediterranean outsider view may suit a Spanish speaker.
snippet_de: Mein Onkel sagt, die Deutschen trinken viel Bier. Aber er trinkt auch viel Bier. Was ist deutsch und was ist normal? Ich weiß es nicht.
snippet_en: My uncle says Germans drink a lot of beer. But he drinks a lot of beer too. What is German and what is normal? I don't know.
aids: German-English glossary after every chapter; comprehension exercises with answers; e-reader tap dictionary works since it's a normal ebook
notes: Snippet taken from a copy of chapter 1 hosted on Scribd (unofficial upload); the Smashwords listing and Google Books confirm title, price and publisher. The series continues across 8+ books in different cities, so it suits serialized reading. Audiobook versions exist for some volumes (not verified).

title: German Short Stories for Beginners (story 1: Die verrückte Currywurst)
author: Olly Richards & Alex Rawlings
format: Ebook and paperback; 8 stories in different genres
level_judgment: Not for a true beginner yet. It mixes tenses and has longer sentences, so plan on it around month 2–3.
genre: Mixed genres: comedy, sci-fi, fantasy, crime, history
hook: Each story is a different genre (a mad currywurst road trip, a creature, a knight, a dragon), which makes it a useful taste-tester.
snippet_de: „Daniel, komm her!“ ruft mir Julia von der Haustür zu. „Was möchtest du, Julia?“, antworte ich. „Heute reisen wir nach Deutschland.“
snippet_en: "Daniel, come here!" Julia calls to me from the front door. "What do you want, Julia?" I answer. "Today we're travelling to Germany."
aids: Bolded hard words with English glossary, plot summaries, comprehension questions; no parallel translation
notes: Snippet taken from a PDF of the original self-published edition hosted on a school site, probably unauthorized. The newer Teach Yourself/Quercus edition 'Short Stories in German for Beginners' (ISBN 9781473683372) has different stories and comes with audio; I didn't verify its text.

title: Gefährliche Spaziergänge (Spannender Lernkrimi)
author: Volker Borbein, Christian Baumgarten / Hueber
price: €8.50 print (PDF/EPUB editions of the series about €7.50)
format: Illustrated booklet, 48 pages + free MP3 audiobook download
level_judgment: Yes from about week 4–6. Short present-tense sentences, with footnote definitions in simple German rather than English.
hook: A lonely Hamburg widow lets a charming stranger into her villa, and the next day her valuable paintings are gone. Her broke grandson is the obvious suspect.
snippet_de: Es ist früh am Morgen. Sophie von Breymann, 68 Jahre, sportlich, kurze graue Haare, liebt die Ruhe um diese Zeit. Es sind nur wenige Autos auf den Straßen.
snippet_en: It's early in the morning. Sophie von Breymann, 68, sporty, short grey hair, loves the quiet at this hour. There are only a few cars on the streets.
aids: Footnote glosses in easy German, colour illustrations, exercises and answer key, full audiobook MP3 (hueber.de/audioservice)
notes: Snippet taken from the publisher's reading sample, mirrored at oxico.sk; Hueber's own sample link loads via JavaScript. Other A1 titles in the same series include 'Du findest mich nicht!' (football murder).

title: Der Grüffelo
author: Julia Donaldson & Axel Scheffler, transl. Monika Osberghaus / Beltz & Gelberg
price: About €10 (board book) to about €15 (standard picture book, ISBN 978-3-407-79230-3)
format: Native picture book (print); many free read-aloud videos and audiobooks exist
level_judgment: Partly. It's very short, but the rhyming verse uses word order and words like flüchtete and Götterspeise that a beginner won't know. Best read alongside the English Gruffalo they may already know.
genre: Children's picture book / humour in verse
hook: A clever mouse bluffs a fox, an owl and a snake with a made-up monster, and then the monster turns up. If the learner knows the English version, they'll know the plot already.
snippet_de: Die Maus spazierte im Wald umher. Der Fuchs sah sie kommen und freute sich sehr. »Hallo, kleine Maus, wohin geht die Reise?«
snippet_en: The mouse strolled around in the wood. The fox saw her coming and was very pleased. "Hello, little mouse, where are you off to?"
aids: None built in; pictures carry the meaning; English original works as a parallel text
notes: Snippet from Beltz's official reading-sample PDF (media.pim.beltz.de). 'Audio: true' refers to commercial audiobook and film versions, not the book itself.

title: Die Sterntaler (Brothers Grimm), bilingual edition
author: Brüder Grimm / grimmstories.com
level_judgment: Too hard to read unaided at A1. It's one long sentence with relative clauses and old-fashioned words (Kämmerchen, fromm). Read the English column first and then the German. Better at around A2.
hook: A one-page tale: a penniless orphan gives away everything and the stars fall as gold coins. It's very short and a canonical piece of German culture.
snippet_de: Es war einmal ein kleines Mädchen, dem war Vater und Mutter gestorben, und es war so arm, dass es kein Kämmerchen mehr hatte, darin zu wohnen. Es war aber gut und fromm.
snippet_en: Once upon a time there was a little girl whose father and mother had died, and she was so poor that she no longer had a little room to live in. But she was good and pious.
aids: Full parallel English translation (choose any language pair, including Spanish)
notes: Snippet trimmed: the first sentence continues, and I joined its first clause to the next sentence. The 1857 original is on Wikisource. Grimmstories lets you pair German with Spanish, which might work better for this learner.

title: MiniKlexikon: Berliner Mauer (plus any other article)
author: MiniKlexikon (ZUM e.V.)
format: Web encyclopedia in very easy German
level_stated: Reading beginners and children learning German as a second language (no CEFR)
level_judgment: Yes from about week 3–4. Short sentences and hyphenated compounds (Säuge-Tiere) make it unusually readable. The sister site Klexikon.zum.de is a step harder (about A2–B1).
hook: Pick any topic the learner already cares about (cats, the Berlin Wall, football, planets) and read a short, real explanation of it. It covers thousands of topics.
snippet_de: Die Berliner Mauer war früher eine Grenze in Berlin. Etwa 30 Jahre lang war Berlin geteilt.
snippet_en: The Berlin Wall used to be a border in Berlin. For about 30 years, Berlin was divided.
aids: None built in; pair with a browser pop-up dictionary
notes: Native material written for native children, so the German is natural rather than textbook German. Good for letting the learner choose their own topics.

title: nachrichtenleicht: Mädchen verletzt sich an Nadel in Halloween-Süßigkeiten
author: Deutschlandfunk (nachrichtenleicht.de)
format: Web news in Easy Language, updated weekly, each article with an audio version
level_judgment: Not in month 1. Topics and words are adult news (Bundes-Land, Gegenstände, Täter). Workable around month 2–3, with audio and a dictionary.
hook: This week's real German news, written simply, which is good for someone who likes keeping up with current events.
snippet_de: In dem Bundes-Land Niedersachsen war zum Beispiel eine Nadel in einem Schoko-Riegel. Eine Mädchen verletzte sich beim Reinbeißen an der Zunge.
snippet_en: In the state of Lower Saxony, for example, there was a needle in a chocolate bar. A girl injured her tongue when she bit into it.
aids: Built-in glossary (Wörterbuch) for hard words; audio for every article
notes: 'Eine Mädchen' is the site's own typo, copied verbatim (correct: 'Ein Mädchen'). Article dated 2 Nov 2026, so it will scroll off the front page.

title: Comic: Ein Tag in Berlin
author: Goethe-Institut (Deutschstunde portal)
level_judgment: Probably yes from about week 3–4: the panels carry the meaning and the speech bubbles are everyday phrases. Not verified, because I couldn't read the comic text.
hook: A diverse group of young friends spend a day out in Berlin: introductions, directions, ordering food. It's a visual tour of present-day Berlin.
snippet_de: No snippet available. Publisher blurb: 'In this comic, learners accompany a diverse group of friends on a day out in Berlin. Everyday communication situations such as introducing themselves, asking for directions, ordering something, etc. are illustrated.'
aids: Pictures; teacher worksheets per chapter; no dictionary
notes: The PDF download (dlapi link) returned 403 Forbidden to curl and failed in Exa. It probably works in a normal browser.

title: Elke und Jonas (graphic novel for beginners)
author: My Generation of Polyglots (transl. Julie Young)
level_judgment: Likely yes from week 2–3, since every German word is glossed on the page. Unverified because I couldn't read the text itself.
hook: A girl moves into a new apartment block and strikes up a friendship with a neighbour. Gentle and low-stakes, with a picture on every page.
snippet_de: No snippet available. Publisher blurb: 'Elke moves into a new apartment complex and develops a friendship with Jonas. The two encourage each other to cultivate new interests and find new friends.'
aids: Every German word defined in English at the foot of each page; un-glossed full text at the end for rereading
notes: Written mainly for US high-school classes. The same publisher sells 'Eine Katze als Hut', a book of short beginner comics ($7.99). The sample-chapter link on the product page was not opened.

title: Die Rache des Computers (Black Cat 'Lesen und Üben')
author: Regine Böttcher, Susanne Lang, Rosi Hinz / Black Cat–Cideb
level_judgment: Too hard for month 1. Aim for it around month 2–3.
hook: A lazy, selfish computer fan loses control of his PC, and a harmless game drags him into a 'trip to hell' with no reset button.
snippet_de: No snippet available. Publisher/retailer blurb (German): 'Sind Computer intelligenter als wir? Für Michael, einen Computerfan wie du und ich, wird ein harmloses Computerspiel zu einer Fahrt in die Hölle. Da funktioniert die Maus nicht mehr und es gibt auch keinen Reset.'
snippet_en: Blurb: 'Are computers smarter than us? For Michael, a computer fan like you and me, a harmless computer game becomes a trip to hell. The mouse stops working and there's no reset either.'
aids: Glossary at the foot of each page, exercises, full audio narration
notes: Blurb taken from languages-direct.com, a retailer. The publisher page has an audio extract.

title: [Separate assessment] LLM-generated personalised graded stories
author: Claude/ChatGPT direct, or apps such as Gradia, NativePal, LibroAI, MeloLingua, Outloud Reader, Next Adventure Reader
price: Free to about $5–13/month (Gradia: $4.99 text / $12.99 audio; MeloLingua Premium: $69/year)
format: Generated on demand in a web app or chat; most apps add TTS audio and tap-to-translate
level_judgment: Possible, but the level needs constraining and checking. Evidence: Uchida (2025) found ChatGPT-4o hit the requested CEFR level in only 5% of 180 English texts zero-shot, and most 'A1/A2' texts came out pre-A1, i.e. too simple, with A1 and A2 barely different. GEM workshop 2023 ('Flesch or Fumble') found ChatGPT tended to write one level too high (B1 when asked for A2). For German specifically, Drackert, Horbach & Peters (2025, ARAL) found ChatGPT texts needed fixing for nominalisations, lexical density, technical vocabulary and anglicised phrasing. A Korean DaF study (Hwang et al. 2025) found simplification to A1/A2 especially weak. 'From Tarzan to Tolkien' (ACL Findings 2024) shows level control improves a lot with few-shot examples or fine-tuning.
hook: It solves the enjoyment problem directly: stories about the learner's own hobbies, job or favourite genre, which no fixed catalogue can do.
snippet_de: No snippet available (generated content; no fixed text to quote).
aids: Most apps: tap-to-translate, sentence translation, TTS audio, vocabulary lists
notes: Verdict: worth using as a supplement once the learner knows a few hundred words, not as the main diet at A0. Make it work by (1) giving the model a word list the learner already knows plus a few new words per story, (2) pasting an example A1 text such as a Duolingo story or MiniKlexikon article, (3) asking for present tense and main clauses only, and (4) having a native or reference check for unnatural, English-flavoured German. None of the apps listed publish evidence of their level accuracy; I only read their marketing pages.
